source.title: Nonconformal Distortion and Local Orientation Reversal in the Fourier Circuit of a Modular-Addition Transformer
source.authors: Eduardo Fuentes; Gonzalo Riera; Héctor Allende-Cid

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes a Fourier-based modular-addition transformer and measures grokking-related accuracy and training dynamics, but its main method is a different measurement: directional Beltrami distortion of a frequency-projected MLP map.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a delayed generalization trajectory for one modular-addition run and tracks a Fourier-circuit metric over training. It does not sweep training-set size. It does not test memorizing-component removal, non-algorithmic tasks, initialization or weight-norm toggles, LLM training, critical dataset size, or optimizer/numerical artifact explanations. Results it cites from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper's main object is Beltrami geometry, a different construct. Its grokking-relevant results come from re-measuring the public Nanda et al. checkpoint series. It locates memorization (epoch 476) before the test-loss transition (2,390–9,830), which bears on V1. It tracks a Fourier-circuit logit-variance metric across 500 checkpoints, which bears on V2. The run is the original source's own, so these are re-analyses, not independent replications.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find nonconformal, spatially organized distortion with local orientation reversal in the frequency-projected MLP maps. Distortion is lower than at initialization and than most random-plane controls, with caveats on overlap and frame conditioning. It recurs across six seeds for most frequencies. It decreases early, before most Fourier-circuit formation, and does not predict per-input correct-logit margins. Temporal ordering is not taken as causal.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures directional Beltrami coefficients of a Fourier-projected MLP map and reuses a publicly released modular-addition checkpoint series; it is not a reproduction of the original grokking intervention or accuracy study.
record.method_sensitivity: Measurements vary with Fourier frequency, input-plane scale, basepoint regime, and checkpoint. The random-plane controls differ in frame conditioning; the paper also reports different orientation-reversal fractions across frequencies and checks a scale range of 0.50–2.00.

fits_no_version.finding: Median Beltrami distortion of the key-frequency projected MLP maps falls from 0.939 at initialization to about 0.39 by epoch 1,400, before generalization onset, then fluctuates. Most of the change precedes circuit-metric growth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local geometric distortion of circuit components settles early, during memorization, before the generalizing circuit forms.

fits_no_version.finding: Beltrami magnitude has negligible correlation with correct-logit margin at epoch 9,400 (|ρ| ≤ 0.026). This is below the preregistered 0.20 threshold and below an embedding-norm baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local distortion does not predict per-input correctness during the grokking transition.

record.problems: The temporal and input-level behavioral analyses use one training run. The study does not sweep training-set size. The random-plane comparison has conditioning differences and limited inferential interpretation; six-run measurements cover only late checkpoints, with two contributed runs lacking checkpoints for independent verification. The Beltrami measure is a two-dimensional section of a projected MLP map, and the authors state that its temporal ordering does not show causality.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; all selected claim-relevant outcomes fit within the row limit.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size (only fraction 0.30 is used).
Later removal of memorizing components; causal link between circuit formation and the jump.
All: no non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
All: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
All: no weight-decay comparison, critical dataset size or ungrokking test.
Six seeds select different key frequencies, but learned algorithms are not identified or compared.
All: no optimizer or floating-point controls.

missing.what: Circuit metric rises from 0.1 to 0.9 during epochs 5,400–11,400. This is the main V2 trajectory and is not a row.
Six independent seeds (same hyperparameters) reach full-pair accuracy of 99.47–100% at epochs 40,000/40,100 with training accuracy 100%. Generalization replicates, but delay timing is not reported.
Test-accuracy trajectory across checkpoints, needed to align the circuit metric with the accuracy jump. Not reported beyond epochs 9,400 and 40,000.

record.verdict_notes: The study reuses the checkpoint series of an original V2 source (Nanda et al.). Its V1/V2 support is therefore a re-analysis of the same run, not an independent replication; weigh accordingly. The reader's V2 limits_scope label rested on Beltrami-margin correlations, which measure a different construct; it is replaced with a timing-based qualification from the circuit metric. The Beltrami rows are moved to fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: The training-set-size dependence, including whether smaller training sets require more optimization, is not tested.
The study does not measure removal of memorizing components or establish that such removal causes generalization. Its one-run temporal analysis does not establish causality.
Non-algorithmic data and initialization-scale or weight-norm switches are not tested.
LLM pretraining and fine-tuning on realistic data are not tested.
No weight-decay comparison, low-norm efficiency test, critical dataset-size prediction, or ungrokking test is reported.
Independent runs are measured for distortion, but the study does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifact explanations.

relationships.condition: Public Nanda et al. checkpoint run, modular addition P=113, training fraction 0.30, weight decay 1 (re-measurement of an original source's run, not independent)
relationships.reason: Memorization at epoch 476 precedes the test-loss transition (2,390–9,830). Test accuracy is 0.51 at epoch 9,400 with training accuracy 1.0, and accuracy is 100% by epoch 40,000 (r1, r2, r3).
relationships.display_finding: Memorization occurred at epoch 476 before a test-loss transition over epochs 2,390–9,830, with training accuracy 1.0 and test accuracy 0.51 at epoch 9,400 before test accuracy reached 100% by epoch 40,000.

relationships.display_finding: The circuit metric rises from 0.0096 at epoch 500 to 0.027 at 2,300 and 0.97 at 40,000, rising from 0.1 to 0.9 over epochs 5,400–11,400.

source_check.reason: Rows r14–r17 document increasing Fourier explained logit variance; Section 3.3 explicitly reports its gradual rise from 0.1 to 0.9 over epochs 5,400–11,400. This supports gradual circuit formation; removal of memorizing components is untested.

relationships.condition: Timing of this circuit metric relative to test-loss transition onset

relationships.display_finding: At test-loss decline onset, epoch 2,390, the metric was about 2.8% of its final value, placing its main development within the transition rather than before onset.
